**Java – A quick primer** | Topic | What you’ll find | |-------|------------------| | **What it is** | Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed with the philosophy “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). It was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released publicly in 1995. | | **Core idea** | Code written in Java compiles into bytecode (`*.class` files), which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). Because the JVM abstracts away underlying hardware/OS details, the same compiled code can execute on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android devices, embedded systems, etc., without modification. | | **Key characteristics** | • **Strongly typed & statically checked** – errors caught early.
• **Platform independent** via JVM.
• **Rich standard library** (java.lang.*, java.util.*, java.io.* …)
• **Automatic memory management** (garbage collector).
• **Multithreading support** built into core APIs.
• **Security sandbox** for applets/web apps (historical use case). | | **Typical applications** | • Enterprise back‑end services (Spring Boot, Jakarta EE).
• Desktop GUI apps (Swing, JavaFX).
• Mobile apps (Android SDK; though Kotlin has largely taken over).
• Embedded / IoT devices (Arduino + Java ME).
• Big‑data processing frameworks (Apache Hadoop, Spark’s Java API). | | **Evolution timeline** | *1991* – Language design starts.
*1995* – JDK 1.0 release (“Sun One”).
*2002* – Java 2 Platform, Standard Edition (J2SE) → renamed Java SE 5.0 (released 2004).
*2018* – Java 9 introduces modules (Project Jigsaw).
*2021+* – Long Term Support releases every six months (e.g., Java 21 LTS). | | **Syntax basics** | ```java
// HelloWorld.java
public class HelloWorld { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(\"Hello, world!\"); } }\n``` | | **Common ecosystem components** | - **Build tools:** Maven, Gradle, Ant.
- **Testing frameworks:** JUnit, TestNG.
- **Dependency injection/frameworks:** Spring, Quarkus, Micronaut.
- **IDE support:** IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans. | | **Learning resources** | • Official docs: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/
• Interactive tutorials: Codecademy, Coursera, Udemy.
• Books: _Effective Java_ (Joshua Bloch), _Head First Java_. | --- ### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | *Is Java still relevant?* | Absolutely—it's one of the most widely used languages worldwide, especially in enterprise environments. | | *How does Java compare to C++?* | Both compile to native binaries but Java relies on the JVM for portability and automatic garbage collection. C++ offers finer control over system resources but requires manual memory handling. | | *Can I write web front‑ends in Java?* | Traditionally not directly; however, technologies like GWT (Google Web Toolkit) transpile Java to JavaScript, and modern full‑stack solutions often pair Java backend with JS frameworks (React/Vue/etc.). | | *Why do some say Java is slow?* | Early versions had performance overhead due to interpretation. Modern JVM implementations include just‑in‑time compilation and sophisticated optimizations, making Java competitive with many other runtimes. | Feel free to ask more specific questions—whether it's about setting up a project, understanding generics, concurrency patterns, or best practices!
